newsitem.title: MEXICO: Telmex sees more rates changes ahead.
newsitem.headline: Telmex sees more rates changes ahead.

text.p: Mexican telephone firm Telefonos de Mexico (Telmex) sees more adjustments to its long-distance rates ahead as it limbers up for competition from next year, director general Jaime Chico Pardo said.
"We have to continue adjusting, it is basic, we cannot hang back," Chico said in a speech Monday at a national convention of the telephone workers' trade union.

"We have a constant rebalancing of rates," he added. "We have been adjusting our long-distance rates, making them more agile, more simple, lowering some and raising others and adjusting the basic charge."
He said discounts in long-distance rates offered by Telmex would benefit the company in the long run.
"The cost for Telmex with regard to reduced revenue is a benefit for our clients," he said. "We end up winning to the extent that clients accept that we are the best option."
Telmex, the current monopoly holder, faces full long-distance competition with various consortiums of Mexican and U.S. firms from 1997.
